interactions.summary: A student tries to reconcile Inferno and Paradiso through a family-versus-individual distinction, and Jiang endorses that as part of the explanation.
Jiang restates his mechanism by opposing heterosexual marriage as an exclusive pair-bond to male homosexual networks he says can spread across multiple lovers and become institutionally powerful.

claims.claim: The student argues that healthy family order serves the individual, whereas the corrupt pattern under discussion is a group using itself to elevate particular members.
Jiang says heterosexual marriage is a compact between only two people, so adding more lovers breaks the bond rather than expanding it into a wider faction.
A student and Jiang distinguish lesbians from male homosexuals, suggesting that the latter are the case Jiang thinks can sustain multiple-lover networks that turn into social power.

signature_moments.moment: Marriage is framed as a closed two-person compact, so the very structure of heterosexual loyalty is used as an argument against scalable faction-building.
signature_moments.source_phrase: a compact between two people and only two people
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang's cleanest restatement of why he thinks heterosexual and homosexual social effects diverge in Dante's logic.

signature_moments.moment: The student's synthesis turns factional power into a question of whether the group serves the person or the person is dissolved into the group.
signature_moments.source_phrase: harness the power of the group to serve them
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the sharpest student compression of Jiang's running argument.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's formulation of heterosexual marriage as an exclusive two-person bond that blocks the extension of loyalty into a larger secret network.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's phrasing about women and men here is broad, culturally loaded, and likely compressed by spontaneous speech; downstream use should preserve that it is a live seminar claim, not a settled analytic category.
